simple.meaning: בְּשׂוֹרָה (bᵉsôwrâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “glad tidings ; by implication, reward for good news.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Samuel 4:10. The surrounding context includes family line, death, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּשׂוֹרָה (H1309) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: glad tidings ; by implication, reward for good news
definitions.full: H1309. besorah בְּשׂרָה noun feminine tidings (compare Arabic see Ba NB 61 ; Sabean בשרן DHM ZMG 1876, 672 ), 2Sam 4:10 3 t.; בְּשׂוֺרָה 18:25 , 27 — 1 good tidings 1Kin 7:9 . 2 tidings, news 2Sam 18:20 , 25 ; with טובה 18:27 . 3 reward for good tidings 2Sam 4:10 ; 18:22 .

occurrences.englishText: when someone told me, ‘Behold, Saul is dead,’ thinking that he brought good news, I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his news.
Joab said to him, “You must not be the bearer of news today, but you must carry news another day. But today you must carry no news, because the king’s son is dead.”
Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said yet again to Joab, “But come what may, please let me also run after the Cushite.”
The watchman cried, and told the king. The king said, “If he is alone, there is news in his mouth.” He came closer and closer.
The watchman said, “I think the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.”

Then they said to one another, “We aren’t doing right. Today is a day of good news, and we keep silent. If we wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come, let’s go and tell the king’s household.”
